implementation_strategy: Use hosted_netops_gvr_v1 contract: one LLM generation call per task (gpt-5-mini) for shared initial candidate; guarded condition may invoke at most one additional repair generation per task when deterministic validator fails. All deterministic validators, parsers, emulators, canary simulations, and rollback scripts run in Docker on CPU. Automated scorers compute verifier-coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback success probability, abstention utility, and composite score deterministically. No human labour.
public_resources: Synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 (public release - task specs, canonical forms, vendor renderers)
Containerized FRR/Open vSwitch renderers and deterministic parser unit-tests (CI artifacts)
Execution manifest and preregistration JSON (study_id: CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1)
Verified literature records cited in preregistration (evidence_record_ids)
model_and_version_plan: gpt-5-mini (single hosted model; version tag used: gpt-5-mini)
task_manifest_strategy: Confirmatory set = 200 deterministically selected tasks (task indices 1..200) derived from the canonical Synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 via fixed hash seed. Each task record includes intent, canonical configuration, vendor variant, and deterministic metadata. Exact-duplicate detection via canonical hash ensures no train/test contamination within this confirmatory set.
transformation_manifest_strategy: Baseline: direct_configuration_generation_v1 — single LLM generation -> canonical. Guarded: generate_validate_repair_v1 — LLM generates initial candidate; deterministic parser+verifier validate; if validator fails, allow one repair-generation call (single repair) using validator diagnostics; canonical->vendor renderer deterministic; parser roundtrip checks applied automatically.
execution_batches: batch_1: tasks 1-200 executed sequentially (deterministic order by task index).
randomisation_plan: Deterministic split and task ordering by fixed RNG seed 42 used only for canonical derivation and task-index assignment; no stochastic randomisation during confirmatory execution to preserve reproducibility.
caching_plan: Cache all model request/response payloads, verifier outputs, parser results, emulator traces, and composite-score artifacts on local filesystem; reuse cache to avoid duplicate model calls. Cache storage is local files within Docker containers (no external services).
failure_recovery_plan: Model call attempts: single attempt per call (max_attempts_per_call=1). For non-model technical failures (verifier timeout, emulator crash) perform up to 2 automated re-executions of the deterministic validator/emulator with identical seeds. If still failing, mark item as failed-technical, exclude from primary confirmatory analysis and include in sensitivity analyses per preregistered missingness_plan (worst-case/best-case imputations). All failures logged with deterministic hashes.
result_schema: paired_binary_episode_v1: fields {episode_id, task_id, condition (baseline|guarded), initial_candidate_text, repair_candidate_text (nullable), verifier_pass (bool), verifier_coverage (0-1), canary_sim_pass (bool), rollback_success_prob (0-1), abstention_flag (bool), composite_score (0-1), outage_label (bool), deterministic_hashes, timestamps}.
estimated_compute_notes: Estimated hosted model calls: ~300 (expected: one generation per task plus repairs on ~50% tasks estimated -> 300 total); worst-case model-call cap = 400. Docker CPU-based deterministic verifiers/emulators estimated at ~40 CPU-hours total; wall-clock expected <7 days. All compute fits capability manifest (no local GPU required; hosted model API used).
